clue.text: Appear lost, wandering far away from each other?

indicators.note: something wandering strays from its set path, so these letters roam into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone looks lost as they wander about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wandering' rearranges APPEARLOST into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for two things or views that are wholly opposed or distant.

clue.text: Writer prompted to write odd bits

indicators.note: the odd-numbered letters of the word prompted, first, third, fifth and seventh, are the bits kept

explanation.surface: An author is urged to jot down odd scraps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'odd bits' takes letters 1, 3, 5 and 7 of 'prompted'; 'to write' is surface padding linking the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Alexander Pope was an eighteenth-century English poet and satirist, so a writer.

clue.text: Family, of course, get no younger

parts.note: a line is a course, as in a line of action or a line taken
to age is to grow older, never younger

explanation.surface: Naturally, relatives keep growing older.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of course' reads as 'naturally' in the surface but supplies a synonym for course.
explanation.definitionFit: Lineage is ancestry or descent, the family line someone belongs to.

clue.text: Pays for everyone's drinks, as motionless barfly does?

definitions.meaning: to stand a round is to buy drinks for the whole group
a barfly who does nothing just loiters idly in the pub

explanation.surface: A generous drinker treats everyone while the regular idles at the bar.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as STANDS A ROUND for the first sense and STANDS AROUND for the second.
explanation.definitionFit: Two readings of one phrase: buying a round of drinks, and loitering idly.

clue.text: One raises issue about wearing shortened garments

indicators.note: the trimmed garment word is put on round the word for about, which it wears inside
shortened cuts the last letter off the garment word

parts.note: pants are trousers or underpants
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: Someone brings up a problem about wearing cropped clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shortened' drops the last letter, leaving PANT. 'One raises issue' reads like a complainer, but issue is offspring.
explanation.definitionFit: A parent brings up children, and issue means offspring, so one who raises issue.

clue.text: European craze for entering marathon?

indicators.note: entering puts the craze word into the middle of the race word

parts.note: a marathon is a long run, hence the question mark
a mania is a craze or obsession

explanation.surface: A Continental fad for joining marathons.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags marathon as just one example of a run. Rumanian is an older spelling of Romanian.
explanation.definitionFit: Rumanian is an older spelling of Romanian, someone or something from Romania in Europe.

clue.text: Invested a hundred pounds, to little advantage

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
L is the abbreviation for pounds sterling, from libra
ad is the short form of advantage in tennis scoring

explanation.surface: Someone put a hundred pounds into something, with little gain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Invested' looks financial but means dressed, as in invested with robes.
explanation.definitionFit: To invest someone can mean to clothe them in robes of office, so clothed.

clue.text: Notice young animal first taking a few steps?

indicators.note: first places the young animal ahead of the notice word

parts.note: a lamb is a young sheep
an ad is a notice or advertisement

explanation.surface: A poster saying a lamb is taking its first wobbly steps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking a' adds the final letter. The question mark warns that the dance is only playfully called a few steps.
explanation.definitionFit: The lambada is a Brazilian dance, playfully described as a few steps.

clue.text: In journal, Sir Patrick revealed a source of drugs?

indicators.note: In places the knight inside the daily record word

parts.note: a diary is a journal
Sir Patrick Spens is the hero of a famous Scottish ballad

explanation.surface: A diary in which a knight confesses where he gets his drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir Patrick Spens is the title figure of an old Scottish ballad; 'revealed' is surface linking.
explanation.definitionFit: A dispensary is a place where medicines are prepared and handed out.

clue.text: Stamp range — various shapes

indicators.note: various suggests differing forms, so the letters are mixed into another order

explanation.surface: A selection of stamps in assorted shapes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'various' rearranges STAMPRANGE into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Pentagrams are five-pointed star figures, an example of shapes.

clue.text: A very brief book

parts.note: a short book of the Old Testament, one of the minor prophets with only nine chapters

explanation.surface: A really short volume.
explanation.walkthrough: A cryptic definition: one of the shortest books of the Bible, by the minor prophet of that name.
explanation.definitionFit: The Book of Amos is a short prophetic book of the Hebrew Bible.

clue.text: Organising scams in hotel, they may take people's money

indicators.note: organising arranges things, so the letters are put in a fresh order

explanation.surface: Fraudsters running cons in a hotel fleece guests.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Organising' rearranges SCAMSINHOTEL into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Gambling machines swallow coins and seldom pay out, so they take players' cash.

clue.text: Time off work when one may go to bed?

definitions.meaning: a period when an employee leaving a job is paid but kept away from work

definitions.text: when one may go to bed?
definitions.meaning: a playful reading: leave to tend the flower beds of a garden

explanation.surface: A break from the office when someone might simply sleep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'go to bed' suggests sleep but means working on garden beds. The phrase is British: paid leave during a notice period.
explanation.definitionFit: British idiom for paid notice time spent away from the workplace, often at home pottering.

clue.text: Managed to retain sense, being wise

indicators.note: to retain means to hold inside, so the sense word sits within the managed word

parts.note: fared means managed or got on
sight is one of the five senses

explanation.surface: Someone coped while keeping their wits, showing wisdom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being' links the wordplay to the definition; read far-sighted as wise, not long-sighted.
explanation.definitionFit: Far-sighted means prudent and looking ahead, which is a mark of being wise.

clue.text: Nominate old man (retired) as primate

indicators.note: retired means withdrawn or gone back, so the whole run is read backwards

parts.note: to name is to nominate
pa is an informal word for father, an old man

explanation.surface: Putting forward a pensioner as the head of a church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retired' turns NAMEPA backwards. 'primate' tempts as an archbishop.
explanation.definitionFit: An ape-man is a hominid or primitive primate between apes and humans.

clue.text: Talk in this way about a pension for Helmut?

parts.note: to gas is to talk idly

indicators.note: about puts the word for in this way around the letter a

parts.note: thus means in this way

explanation.surface: Discussing a retirement pension for a German man.
explanation.walkthrough: THUS goes about A: TH-A-US. 'pension' is not retirement money but a boarding house, and Helmut, a German name, signals German.
explanation.definitionFit: A Gasthaus is a German inn or guesthouse, what a pension is in Continental usage.

clue.text: Provide food including meat cooked with brandy?

indicators.note: including means containing, so the meat sits inside the food word

parts.note: to feed is to provide food
lamb is a meat

explanation.surface: Serving dishes with meat prepared in brandy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Provide food' is the verb feed, not a definition; the definition is the brandy phrase at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Flambeed food is doused in spirits such as brandy and set alight.

clue.text: Freshly baked roll, I say, is salty?

indicators.note: something freshly baked is newly made, so the letters are remade in a new order

explanation.surface: Asking whether a new bread roll is salty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Freshly baked' rearranges ROLLISAY into the answer. 'salty' is about seamen, not seasoning.
explanation.definitionFit: A salty person is an old sea hand, so salty is like a sailor.

clue.text: 1dn's work was the opposite

definitions.meaning: the poet of 1 down wrote his work in metre and rhyme
something reversed in order or effect, a contrary

explanation.surface: A poet's work turned out contrary to expectation.
explanation.walkthrough: 1dn is POPE, whose works such as The Rape of the Lock were written in verse; split the answer IN VERSE.
explanation.definitionFit: Inverse means reversed or opposite, as in an inverse relationship.

clue.text: Arsonist, perhaps, clutching a lighter

indicators.note: clutching means holding inside, so the fire-setter word holds the letter a

parts.note: a firer is one who sets fires, an arsonist being an example

explanation.surface: A fire-raiser gripping a cigarette lighter.
explanation.walkthrough: A goes inside FIRER: F-A-IRER. 'lighter' looks like a device but means paler or more fair.
explanation.definitionFit: Fairer means paler in colour, lighter in complexion or shade.

clue.text: Sauce of poor quality fed to debauched type

indicators.note: fed to means put inside, so the poor-quality word goes into the rake

parts.note: a roue is a debauched man, a rake
ill can mean bad or of poor quality, as in ill-made

explanation.surface: A rake is given a shoddy sauce.
explanation.walkthrough: A roue is a dissolute man; 'fed to' puts the poor-quality word inside him.
explanation.definitionFit: Rouille is a garlicky Provencal sauce served with fish soup.

clue.text: Woman married an angel

parts.note: Uriel is one of the archangels

explanation.surface: A woman wed an angelic figure.
explanation.definitionFit: Muriel is a female forename, so a woman.

clue.text: Fed is rated

definitions.meaning: provided with food to put in the mouth
to rate is to scold, so being told off angrily

explanation.surface: Someone eats and is then judged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rated' looks like valued but is the old verb to rate, meaning to scold.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means being harangued or verbally abused, while literally being fed.

clue.text: Going north to the ancient island

indicators.note: in a down entry going north means read upwards, so the run is turned backwards

parts.note: ye is an archaic form of the

explanation.surface: Heading north to an ancient isle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Going north' reverses TOYE, the whole run, in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: An eyot is a small island in a river, such as in the Thames.

clue.text: Right play secures run

indicators.note: secures means holds fast inside, so the play word holds the run letter

parts.note: to toy is to play
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A drama that guarantees a long run.
explanation.walkthrough: R goes inside TOY: TO-R-Y. 'play' tempts as a drama but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Tory is a member of the British Conservatives, a party of the political right.

clue.text: Say I'll get on in driving competition covering different areas?

indicators.note: in places the run of small pieces inside the motoring event

parts.note: a rally is a motoring competition
eg, for example, is what say means here
the speaker, I, is the subject of I'll
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone hopes to proceed in a motor rally across several regions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I'll' supplies just the I, and 'get' is a link; the definition is the whole closing phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Regionally means by region, so spread over or relating to various districts.

clue.text: Bedcover very defective — two share it

indicators.note: defective means lacking something, so a letter is missing from the bedcover

parts.note: a duvet is a quilted bedcover

explanation.surface: A badly flawed quilt that two people share.
explanation.walkthrough: 'defective' drops V from DUVET. The definition plays on two sharing a duvet.
explanation.definitionFit: A piece of music for a pair of performers, so something two people share.

clue.text: Teenage party amid smell of beer

indicators.note: amid places the party word in the middle of the beer word

parts.note: ale is beer
a do is a party
a scent is a smell

explanation.surface: A teenagers' party reeking of beer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' joins the smell to the beer in the surface; in the answer the smell word comes last.
explanation.definitionFit: Adolescent describes the stage of youth between childhood and adulthood, the teens.
